bars: 8 of 8 cases pass in the new test: behind on main moved; uncommitted work only warned (twice, the edit kept); merged branch switched to main; stale branch with own commits warned, not moved; fresh branch told it is behind; up to date silent; web clone left alone; hook and resume print it as their first line
stale means no commit for 2 days while the trunk moved (the harmonize gap: 11-22 to 11-24)
body:
A session on your computer now starts on the newest code from GitHub: at session start (and at the first resume of any role) the kit fetches and, when the checkout is clean and on main or on a branch already merged into it, moves it forward by itself. When it holds work of its own (uncommitted changes, or commits not on main) it never moves it: the first line says it is behind or stale and what to run.

### What happens at start
The SessionStart hook runs `kit.py fresh` (fetch of the trunk only, 25 s at most) and puts its line first; `kit.py resume` does the same before anything else, the first time in a session (a mark per session id in .kit/run/fresh/). Later resumes look again without fetching and repeat only a line that still asks something (uncommitted work, own commits on the trunk, a stale branch).

### The cases
| checkout | what the kit does |
|---|---|
| on main, clean, behind | fast-forward to origin/main, one line says how many commits and the newest |
| branch merged into main (no commit of its own), clean | switch to main (created tracking origin/main if absent), fast-forward |
| behind, uncommitted changes | not moved; says to commit or stash, then the merge to run |
| main with commits not on origin | not moved; `git pull --no-rebase`, then push |
| branch with own commits, no commit for 2+ days while main moved | not moved; stale: merge origin/main or finish it |
| branch with own commits, recent | told it is behind and what is newer; not moved |
| web session (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE, KIT_REMOTE, AGY_REMOTE) | nothing: the clone is fresh |
| fetch fails | one line: could not fetch, the code may be old |

Untracked files do not count as uncommitted work (git refuses a move that would overwrite one anyway). The old SessionStart line (CLONE: behind its upstream, no fetch) stays only where .kit/kit.py is absent.

### Where
`checkout_fresh` and `checkout_fresh_once` in scripts/kit.py, the `fresh` command (listed in `kit.py commands`), kit/hooks/kit_session_start.py, tests/test_checkout_fresh.py.
handoff: The orchestrator's real-project run: open a session in ~/harmonize (on agy-board-install or any branch behind main) and see the first line say CHECKOUT and, when clean and merged, the checkout land on origin/main. The command is `kit.py fresh` (`--again` to run it now, past the once-a-session mark in .kit/run/fresh/).
not_checked: the real run on ~/harmonize (the orchestrator's, per the launch: this session attaches no repo)
a Windows checkout: the code is plain git calls with no shell, but it ran here on Linux only

task:
A session always starts on the newest code from GitHub, in every checkout: the rule "use git" covers the board's data (reconcile at start) and parts (6b69f1e: a part starts on its step's newest work), but not a project's own checkout. ~/harmonize sat on branch agy-board-install from 11-22 while Harmonize's main on GitHub had moved on (0d020efb, 11-24): a session opened there, and the kit's own real-project check, worked on two-day-old code with nothing saying so.

1. At `board` start and at the first resume of any role, the kit fetches origin and says, before anything else, when this checkout is behind its trunk or sits on a branch that is merged or stale (no commit for N days while the trunk moved): one line with what is newer.
2. When the checkout is clean and its branch is the trunk or merged into it, it moves forward by itself (fast-forward, or switch to the trunk); with uncommitted work or commits of its own, it never moves it: it says what to do, and resume names it as the first thing.
3. The same on every platform (a web clone is fresh already: nothing to do there), with a test: a clone behind origin is moved forward at start; one with uncommitted work is only warned.
title: A session always starts on the newest code from GitHub, in every checkout
verdict: Done: a checkout behind GitHub is moved forward at start when that loses nothing, and otherwise warned in the first line; the ~/harmonize case (a merged branch two days behind main) now switches to main by itself.
